articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built ScopeShield is a local AI assistant that helps freelancers identify scope creep before agreeing to additional client work. Every freelancer knows the situation: a project starts with a clear brief, but new requests gradually appear. A client asks for another feature, extra revisions, content migration, or work that was never included in the original agreement. Freelancers must decide whether the request is already covered, needs clarification, or should be discussed as additional work. Handling this repeatedly takes time and can create uncomfortable client conversations.

articles.title: Processing XML in PostgreSQL: Do You Really Need PL/Python?
articles.excerpt: In my previous article, I explained how a university assignment led me to run Python inside PostgreSQL to validate XML documents against an XSD. It worked. I completed the assignment, learned somethin…
articles.body: In my previous article , I explained how a university assignment led me to run Python inside PostgreSQL to validate XML documents against an XSD. It worked. I completed the assignment, learned something new about PostgreSQL, and moved on. Two years later, I revisited the project with a different question in mind: how much of that solution actually needed Python? PostgreSQL already provides functions for generating XML, querying its contents, and extracting values into relational columns. What it doesn't provide natively is validation against an arbitrary XML Schema Definition (XSD). But while reviewing the original files, I found something I hadn't fully appreciated at the time. Some XML documents produced by the SQL query didn't satisfy the very XSD they were supposed to follow.

articles.title: I Used to Think Software Testing Was Unnecessary. Then I Started Building My Own Project.
articles.excerpt: I used to think writing unit tests, E2E tests, and maintaining a proper testing suite was unnecessary for most projects. If developers write the code, can't they just test it themselves? For a long ti…
articles.body: I used to think writing unit tests, E2E tests, and maintaining a proper testing suite was unnecessary for most projects. If developers write the code, can't they just test it themselves? For a long time, that made sense to me. Until I started building something of my own. How It Started At the end of June, I started building The Last Deploy — an open-source platform where people can learn DevOps and Platform Engineering through hands-on labs. In the beginning, I made a lot of decisions based on one thing: If it works, ship it. I'll fix it if something breaks. I even coded directly on the production server for a while. Not because it was a good engineering practice, but because it felt faster.

articles.body: Every time I built data-intensive systems in .NET, handling bulk data ingestion always felt fragmented. Different databases required completely different boilerplate, performance quirks, and error-handling strategies. So I spent the week solving it cleanly from first principles. I’m excited to introduce FastIngest: a modular, high-throughput bulk ingestion framework for .NET. Published completely open source under the permissive MIT license. Instead of writing provider-specific bulk copy hacks for every new project, FastIngest gives developers a unified, highly optimized API designed for heavy write loads and streaming pipelines.

articles.excerpt: "Just like here on Earth, Mars helicopters can cover distance quickly and can go places that might be impossible to reach by ground."
articles.body: NASA is accelerating the development of three helicopters that will be deployed into the sky above Mars after a voyage aboard NASA's Space Reactor‑1 Freedom spacecraft. Slated for launch in 2028, SR-1 Freedom is the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft and is assigned the duty of dropping off the SkyFall entry capsule loaded with the trio of aerial vehicles at the Red Planet. SR-1's trajectory will deliver the SkyFall helicopters in Mars' northern hemisphere during the planet's spring season to avoid dust storms . SkyFall is based on the success of the first aerial craft to float about the Red Planet , Ingenuity , which flew over 70 missions at Jezero Crater before it finally broke a rotor . It was designed to fly five.

articles.title: An Israeli firm is sending spyware through online ads, researchers say
articles.excerpt: An Israeli ad tech firm worked with spyware companies to infect devices, including at Al Jazeera, by simply showing users an online ad, according to a joint investigation by security researchers at Ci…
articles.body: An Israeli ad tech firm worked with spyware companies to infect devices, including at Al Jazeera , by simply showing users an online ad, according to a joint investigation by security researchers at Citizen Lab and Confiant . It's the first time researchers have found technical evidence of a zero-click attack - a form of hacking that requires no action by users - delivered through targeted advertising, as reported earlier by NBC News . The ad firm, called Discover-Tech, presents itself as a typical online advertising agency, but researchers say it actually provides a pipeline for hacking groups to plant malicious ads across the web. articles.excerpt: A Tesla crossed the grass median of Route 55 in New Jersey, hit a tree, slid into oncoming traffic, and struck an SUV head-on. The SUV’s driver, 68-year-old Phillip Eastman, was killed. Police reporte…
articles.body: A Tesla crossed the grass median of Route 55 in New Jersey, hit a tree, slid into oncoming traffic, and struck an SUV head-on. The SUV’s driver, 68-year-old Phillip Eastman, was killed. Police reported it as a driver who lost control. What they didn’t say, and likely didn’t know, is that Tesla’s own report to federal regulators says the car’s driver-assist system was engaged. This is part of an ongoing Electrek investigation matching reported crashes to Tesla’s redacted NHTSA data. more…
